To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) users are able to improve retrieval performance by reformulating their queries, (b) the best way to support query reformulation is to provide users with term suggestions that are both relevant and useful for reformulation, (c) the best way for users to reformulate is to use an interface that allows users to see both their original query and the reformulated query side by side, and (d) the most useful and relevant term suggestions come from a combination of term expansion, query expansion,

the following are the most important factors for supporting interactive query refinement: (a) the quality of the term suggestions, (b) a clear and consistent interface that supports the user in the task at hand, (c) a clear and unambiguous representation of the query and its results, (d) a clear and simple representation of the term suggestion, and (e) the ability to see and understand the relationship between the suggested terms and the query.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to design effective interfaces to support the iterative exploration and reformulation of queries in interactive information retrieval systems.
how people use search engines to reformulate queries.
the design of effective interactive information retrieval systems, and with the evaluation of the effectiveness of the techniques used to support the user in the interactive task.

we have learned that it is very difficult to support interactive query reformulation.

the iterative approach to investigation and evaluation is effective, but that the results of each iteration should be used as the starting point for the next iteration, and not as the final conclusion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the iterative exploration, design, and evaluation of support systems can provide valuable insights into the design and development of usable and useful systems, and that this methodology is especially valuable in the design of support for interactive information retrieval systems.
the iterative approach we have used to investigate and evaluate the support for query reformulations has been successful.
we have developed an effective term suggestion algorithm, and an effective interface for its presentation, and that we have learned a great deal about the relationship between these two.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is important for researchers to develop a clear understanding of their users and their needs before developing and evaluating interactive information retrieval systems, and to use this knowledge to guide the development of the systems and their evaluation.
iterative exploration of design and evaluation of interactive IR systems is a powerful method of understanding the design space and developing usable systems.

it is possible to develop a usable and useful interactive information retrieval system, and that the development process can be guided by a series of small, iterative studies that build on each other, and that lead to a usable system.
